_readme: Short text lines the game picks from at random. No AI needed. Each section has a _default list; add a list under a personality name to give that personality its own lines.
Placeholders: {name}, {house}, plus any extra ones noted for the section. Add as many lines as you like.
enc_* lines are short notes on how one client visit went for her (shown in the weekly report). job_* lines are report lines for the non-escort jobs.
encore: the line added when a restless lady goes another round. enc_frustrated / enc_drained / enc_like / enc_put_off: extra visit notes.
demo_lead / demo_watch: your demonstration lesson ({name} = your partner). Templates; rewrite freely.
orgy_lead ({names}, {first}, {house}), orgy_pair ({a}, {b}), orgy_end ({first}), orgy_lover ({name}: a Devoted lady sharing you): your group nights. Templates; rewrite freely.

gift_trinket / gift_jewel / gift_lavish ({name}, {gift} = a random trinket from people.json gifts): you buy her a gift with gold (her sheet → Gifts). tutor_note ({name}, {tutor}): her weekly report note when a tutor works with her. Templates; rewrite freely.

solo._note: Report line when a lady at max lust spends part of her night alone in her room instead. Shown in the weekly report.
_default: {name} disappeared to her room early one night and didn't come back down for a long while. She seemed a lot calmer afterward.
{name} locked her door for most of an evening. She came out flushed, relaxed, and tired.
Shy but earnest: {name} excused herself early one night, too embarrassed to say why. She avoided everyone's eyes at breakfast.
{name} spent an evening shut in her room with the curtains drawn. She insists she was reading.
Bookish and curious: {name} took a novel of the steamier sort up to her room and was not seen again that night.
{name} called it 'research' and locked her door. She came out with a very satisfied look and ink on her fingers.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} vanished one evening without explanation. When she returned, she was smiling to herself and offered none.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} decided she didn't need anyone's help with her problem, thank you, and took the evening to herself.
{name} snapped at two clients, then went to her room and slammed the door. An hour later she came out in a far better mood.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} figured the easiest solution was the one that didn't involve getting out of bed. She skipped most of one evening.
Calm and elegant: {name} retired early one evening for 'a long bath'. It was a very long bath.

modest._note: Shown on her sheet when she has the Modest trait.
_default: She'd rather keep her clothes on. When things get intimate, they get pulled aside instead, though the lewder she gets (and the more she trusts you), the more comes off.
She keeps her clothing on as long as she can, and she's quietly flustered if it slips. With you, though, she lets the bits come off by degrees, one at a time, when she's ready.
A towel, a sleeve, a half-drawn curtain: she always has something between herself and the lamplight. The more she trusts you, the thinner the barriers get.
She prefers to keep a layer or two on, thank you, and you've learned not to tease about it. Over time, with enough warmth and enough patience, she grows braver.
She's shy about being seen, so the lamps are dimmed and the blankets drawn up. When she finally lets one fall, it feels like a gift.
Her clothes stay mostly on, tugged aside rather than shed. The more comfortable she becomes, the more she reveals, and you notice every inch of progress with a quiet, private joy.
{name} is still breathing hard, and she hasn't let go of you. "Again," she says. It isn't really a question.
{name} props herself up on one elbow and gives you a long, considering look. Apparently you're not finished.
"Don't you dare fall asleep," {name} whispers, pulling you back down against her. The lamp is guttering and the night is long, and she isn't remotely finished with you.
{name} gives a slow, satisfied sigh, stretches like a cat, and then turns that sleepy, dangerous smile on you again. "That was lovely," she says. "I'd like to do it properly now."
You're reaching for the blanket when {name} catches your wrist and shakes her head, smiling. Her cheeks are flushed, her hair is wild, and she looks much too pleased with herself to stop.
For a long moment the only sounds are the rain and your breathing. Then {name} laughs softly, rolls over, and tugs you closer. "One more," she says. "I might even mean it."
{name}'s tail hasn't stopped moving. She nuzzles into your neck, warm and insistent, and makes a small, needy sound that says she's nowhere near done.
{name} is up on her knees before you've caught your breath, ears forward, eyes bright. "More," she says, and climbs back into your lap.

{name}'s ears flick toward you, and her tail curls around your leg and holds on. She purrs, low and rumbling, and presses her forehead to your chest. It's clear the night isn't over until she says so.

A low, contented rumble fills the room as {name} nuzzles into the crook of your neck, tail thumping slowly against the sheets. She's warm, and pleased, and completely unwilling to let you go anywhere.

{name}'s tail sweeps across the blanket in a long, lazy arc, and her eyes shine gold in the lamplight. "Mm," she says, and climbs on top of you with unshakable purpose. You give up the idea of sleeping altogether.
Her ears twitch at every sound, but {name} is fixed on you alone, nosing at your jaw, her breath warm and fast. "Again," she says, in the plain way of someone who has no intention of discussing it.

late_visit._note: Opening line when a lady knocks on your door late at night.
_default: You're doing the books by candlelight when {name} knocks. She hasn't seen a single client all week, and she's clearly been thinking about something. "Busy?"
{name} appears in your doorway in her nightclothes, holding two cups of tea she clearly has no intention of drinking.
A note slides under your door: "Still awake? Come find out." It's in {name}'s handwriting.

The house is quiet, the corridor lamps burning low, when you hear the faintest scratch at your door. It's {name}, barefoot, with a shawl over her shoulders and a look that says she wasn't going to knock but couldn't help it. "Can I come in?" she asks.

You're half asleep over a stack of invoices when {name} lets herself in, carrying a plate of leftover dumplings. "You missed supper," she says, setting it down. She doesn't leave, and she doesn't pretend that the dumplings were the only reason she came.

A soft knock, then another, a little braver. {name} stands in your doorway with a candle, the flame bending in the draft, and her hair loose in a way you haven't seen before. "I couldn't sleep," she says. "I thought you might be awake too."
Shy but earnest: There's a very quiet knock. {name} is standing in the hall, red to the ears, and has clearly rehearsed what she wants to say. She forgets all of it.
Bold and flirtatious: {name} doesn't knock. She just leans in your doorway until you notice her. "You work too hard, boss."

sleepin_evening._note: Opening line when the lady sharing your bed in the Owner's Suite proposes as you turn in. Edit freely.
_default: The lamps are low in the Owner's Suite. {name} sits on the edge of the bed, unpinning her hair, and watches you over her shoulder. "We could just sleep," she says. "Or not."
{name} slides under the blanket and doesn't turn her back on you tonight. Her hand finds yours. "Stay up a little longer," she murmurs.
"Long day," {name} says, curling against your side in the dark. Her fingers start tracing slow circles on your chest. "I have a better idea than sleeping."

The Owner's Suite is warm, the shutters latched against the night wind, and {name} is brushing out her hair at the bedside. She catches your reflection in the dark window and doesn't look away. "I'm not tired," she says, setting down the brush. "Are you?"

{name} blows out the last lamp but one and slips beneath the blanket, her feet cold and her smile warm. Rain whispers on the roof, and she rolls toward you. "Tell me about your day," she says. "Then I'll tell you about mine, and we'll see."
You're mid-yawn when {name} puts a finger over your mouth. The room is lit by a single candle and the pale spill of the two moons through the curtain. "That yawn," she says, "is a lie. I can tell."

sleepin_morning._note: Opening line when the lady sharing your bed wakes you in the morning with ideas of her own. Edit freely.
_default: You wake to gray morning light and {name} propped on one elbow beside you, smiling like she's been awake a while. "Good morning," she says, and kisses you slowly.
Something warm presses against your back, and {name}'s voice is a sleepy whisper at your ear. "Don't get up yet. I've got plans for you."
{name} has already pulled the covers over both your heads. "The house can wait," she says, "for a little while."

A bird is arguing with itself outside the window and the light is the soft pink of early dawn. {name} is already awake, tracing the line of your jaw with one finger. "Don't say anything," she murmurs. "Just stay."

The bed is warm, the house is still asleep, and {name} has her cheek against your shoulder, listening to you breathe. When you stir, she lifts her head with a lazy, knowing smile. "Good," she says. "You're up."

You wake to the smell of baking bread drifting up from the kitchen and {name}'s hair spread over your arm. She doesn't open her eyes. "Five more minutes," she says, in a voice that makes it clear what she plans to do with them.

client_yes._note: Second half of a report highlight when a client got the service he asked for.
_default: They disappeared upstairs for most of the evening.
He came downstairs an hour later looking dazed and very satisfied.
The door stayed closed a long time. He tipped generously.
She came back down first, humming. He followed, red-faced and grinning.
The lamp in the upstairs window burned late, and the piano downstairs had finished two full sets before the door finally opened.
He went up with a nervous cough and a rumpled hat, and came down an hour later carrying the hat and no memory of where he'd left his dignity.
Somewhere between the second glass of plum wine and the stairs, he made up his mind. The staircase creaked for a while afterward, and nobody pretended not to notice.
They slipped away from the crowded lounge while the fiddler was mid-song. By the time the tune ended, the evening had gone somewhere much quieter.
He spent a long, unhurried evening behind a closed door and emerged looking like a man who'd forgotten what day it was. His coin purse, on the other hand, remembered perfectly.
The room smelled of lavender and warm candle wax by the time they were done, and the bedsheets looked like they'd lost an argument.

client_company._note: Second half of a report highlight when a client only wanted her company.
_default: He left lighter in the purse and very happy about it.
He promised to come back next week.
He told three friends about her before he got home.
He lingered on the stairs, patting his pockets like a man who didn't want to leave, then bought a bottle of wine for the road.
He stopped to straighten his collar in the hallway mirror and caught himself smiling at his own reflection.
He paid, he tipped, and he tried to tip again at the door. Sam had to gently steer him outside.
He left humming a tune from the lounge and walked straight into a lamppost. He apologized to it.
He lingered over his last cup of tea in the lounge, reluctant to let the night end, and asked the doorman which evenings were quietest.
He wrote her a small, terrible poem on a napkin before he left. She kept it.

lover_waiting._note: Opening line when a lover (Devoted) at max lust comes to you instead of handling it herself.
_default: {name} is sitting on the edge of your bed when you get back, shoes off, very much not reading the book in her lap. "You've been busy all week," she says. "I've been patient."
You find a note on your desk in {name}'s handwriting: "My room. Tonight. Don't make me come get you."
{name} has made herself comfortable in your chair, feet up on your desk, reading your ledger upside down with great ceremony. "Your handwriting is awful," she announces. "Come here. I've missed you."

The lamp in {name}'s window is lit when you pass her door, and the door is open a hand's width, which is as close to a summons as she'll ever write down. You stop. She says, from inside, "Don't pretend you didn't see."

There's a tray on your bed when you return: tea, two cups, and a single flower in a water glass. {name} is sitting beside it, trying very hard to look casual. "I thought we might have some time," she says. "If you're not busy."
{name} intercepts you on the stairs, takes your sleeve, and doesn't say a word until you're at her door. "Everyone is very busy," she says then. "I decided you could be busy in here."
Shy but earnest: {name} hovers in your doorway, fidgeting with her sleeve. "I, um. I waited. For you. All week." She's bright red.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} corners you in the hall. "I don't beg," she says. "So you're going to notice on your own that it's been a week."

lover_reunion._note: First line of the scene when you go to a lover who's been waiting.
_default: She pulls you in by the collar and doesn't let go for a long time.
"Finally," she breathes, and the door clicks shut behind you both.
She's been counting the hours, and it shows in the way she crosses the room: quickly, then slowly, as if she's remembered she's supposed to be composed. It lasts about a second.
"You're late," she says, with absolutely no heat. Then she kisses you, and neither of you mentions it again.
The lamp is low, the room is warm, and she's waiting for you with her arms already open. You walk into them like a man coming home.
She hooks a finger through your belt and leads you in without a word. The door shuts, the latch drops, and the corridor is left to its rumors.

good_night._note: Report line after a week where her clients loved her.
_default: {name} had a great week and knows it. She's in a very good mood.
Cheerful and teasing: {name} spent breakfast bragging about her week to anyone who'd listen, with impressions of her clients.
Shy but earnest: {name} didn't say much, but she kept smiling to herself all week. Someone said she did well and she turned bright red.
Proud and sharp-tongued: {name} reminded everyone, twice, that she is the best in the house. Nobody argued.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} has started keeping a tally of satisfied clients on the kitchen wall. She's winning.
Bookish and curious: {name} has notes on what worked this week. Detailed notes. She'd like to discuss them.
Warm and motherly: {name}'s clients left happy, and she made a point of making sure the other girls did too.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} said nothing about her week. Her clients said plenty.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} had a good week with surprisingly little effort, which she considers the ideal week.

bad_night._note: Report line after a rough week with unhappy or difficult clients.
_default: {name} had a rough week. A couple of clients left unhappy, and so did she.
Shy but earnest: {name} had a bad client this week and has been very quiet since. She keeps apologizing for nothing.
Proud and sharp-tongued: Two of {name}'s clients complained. {name} complained louder, and is now refusing to speak to anyone.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} took a bad week personally. She's been training twice as hard out of spite.
Cheerful and teasing: {name} laughed off a bad client, but the jokes have been a little thinner this week.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} had a bad week and shrugged it off. Mostly.
Mysterious and aloof: Something about this week bothered {name}. She won't say what.

lover_jealous._note: When one of your lovers has been left out for weeks while another hasn't. {other} = the other lover.
_default: {name} has noticed exactly how many evenings you've spent with {other} lately, and exactly how many you've spent with her. She'd like to talk.
Shy but earnest: {name} hasn't said anything. She's just been very quiet whenever {other} is around, and you finally notice.
Proud and sharp-tongued: "I'm not jealous," {name} announces, apropos of nothing, while glaring at {other} across the room.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} has started treating {other} like a rival. Breakfast has become very tense.

lover_shared._note: When two happy lovers come to your room together. {other} = the second lover.
_default: There's a knock at your door. It's {name}. Then a second knock: {other}, right behind her. They look at each other, then at you, and seem to reach an understanding without you.
{name} and {other} arrive at your door together, arm in arm, as though they'd rehearsed it. They probably did. "We have an arrangement," {name} says, and {other} nods solemnly, hiding a grin.
You open your door to find {name} and {other} in the corridor, whispering. They stop the moment they see you and share a look that says everything. "We'd like to come in," {other} says. "Both of us."

{other} comes in first, shy and a little flushed, and {name} follows close behind to shut the door. They exchange a glance of perfect understanding, which leaves you out of it entirely. You decide not to mind.
"No arguments," {name} says, steering {other} by the elbow into your room. "We've settled it between ourselves." {other} just smiles, wickedly, and sits on the bed.

Two sets of footsteps in the corridor, one knock, and then {name} and {other} are standing in your doorway, giggling like conspirators. Whatever they have planned, they've clearly been planning it for days.

breakup._note: When you end things with a lover. She stays on at the house.
_default: {name} listens without interrupting. "Okay," she says finally. "I'll be fine. Just... give me some time."
Shy but earnest: {name} nods too fast and says she understands, then excuses herself. Nobody sees her for the rest of the day.
Proud and sharp-tongued: "Fine," {name} says crisply. "Your loss." She makes it all the way to the hallway before her voice cracks.
Warm and motherly: {name} squeezes your hand. "You're allowed to change your mind, love. I'm not going anywhere." She cries later, alone.
Hot-blooded and competitive: {name} throws a cup at the wall. Then she apologizes to the cup. Then she leaves.
Laid-back and lazy: {name} shrugs a little too casually. "Sure. Whatever works." She doesn't come down for dinner.
Mysterious and aloof: {name} says nothing at all. She just looks at you for a long moment, then nods once and goes.

rekindle_yes._note: When an ex-lover agrees to try again.
_default: {name} pretends to think about it for exactly three seconds. "Took you long enough."
{name} looks at you for a long while, then lets out a breath she seems to have held for weeks. "Yes," she says. "Obviously yes. Don't make that face, you're going to cry."
"I was hoping you'd ask," {name} admits, smiling in a way that goes straight to her eyes. "I'd have asked you myself, but I wanted to see you work for it."
{name} takes your hand in both of hers. "I've missed this," she says quietly. "I've missed you. Yes. Let's try again."
{name} pretends to consider, tapping her chin and looking out the window. It lasts about a breath and a half before she gives up and kisses you. "Yes, you idiot."
"Fine," {name} says, trying very hard to look put-upon and failing completely. "But you're buying dinner. Several dinners."

rekindle_no._note: When an ex-lover isn't ready to try again.
_default: {name} smiles, a little sadly. "Not yet. Ask me again sometime."
{name} shakes her head gently, her eyes soft. "I care about you," she says, "but I'm not there yet. Give me some time, and be patient with me."
"Not today," {name} says, with a small, sincere smile. "It isn't you. I just need to be sure, and I'm not, not quite. Ask me again."
{name} looks down at her hands for a moment, then up. "I'm sorry," she says. "Part of me wants to say yes. The rest of me needs more time."
She touches your arm briefly, kindly, and lets go. "Ask me again when the leaves turn," {name} says. "I'll have a better answer, I promise."
{name} sighs, not unkindly. "I'm flattered. Really. But I'd be saying yes for the wrong reasons, and you deserve better than that."
She enjoyed that one.
Her favorite. She was humming afterward.
She came back downstairs smiling.
This was the one she'd have picked from the whole week, and she hummed the entire way back to her room.
She stretched out on the cushions afterward looking wonderfully pleased with herself.
She told Sam later it was the best part of her week. Sam turned very red and said he was glad.
She took her time on the stairs afterward, in no hurry to get back to work.
She was still smiling when the next lantern was lit.
Easily her favorite of the week. She kept replaying it over her tea.

enc_dislike._note: Client asked for something she dislikes but does.
_default: Not her favorite.
She got through it, but it's not her thing.
She was a little quiet afterward.
She gave him a perfectly professional evening and kept her real opinion to herself.
She counted the minutes against the candle and was glad when it was over.
She went back to her room afterward and brewed herself something strong.
She kept her smile painted on, but it took some effort.
She wasn't rude about it, but she was quick to change the subject afterward.
She was very careful not to look at the clock, and very glad to wash up after.

enc_stretch._note: A service that's still a stretch for her with clients.
_default: A stretch for her. She did it anyway.
She wasn't sure about it, and it showed a little.
Outside her comfort zone, but she managed.
It wasn't what she'd usually choose, but she gave it an honest try with a brave smile.
She took a deep breath at the door and went in determined to be professional.
Not her usual territory by a long shot, but she muddled through with good humor.
She learned something new about her limits, and decided she could live with it.
A little awkward, a little bold, and she had to laugh at herself halfway through.
She'd rather have been elsewhere, but she held her head up and finished the job.

enc_eager._note: She was in the mood (high lust).
_default: She'd been wanting it all week.
She was more into it than he was.
She was very much in the mood.
She was practically waiting at the door for him.
She'd been eyeing the clock all afternoon and was ready the moment the bell rang.
She'd braided flowers into her hair for the occasion and was not at all shy about it.
She didn't need coaxing; if anything, she was the one doing the leading.
She'd been in a good mood since breakfast and it showed.
Her enthusiasm caught him a little off guard, and then caught him entirely.
He left glowing.
He's already asking when she's free next.
He tipped well and said so twice.
He floated down the stairs with a grin he couldn't wipe off, and walked out into the night humming.
He left a tip big enough that Sam checked it twice for mistakes.
He paid for a bottle for the whole lounge on his way out.
He squeezed her hand at the door and promised to be back before the week was out.
He told the doorman that this was the best night of his life, then corrected it to 'month' and then 'year'.
He looked ten years younger and walked a little taller on the way home.
He left grumbling.
It didn't really click.
Neither of them enjoyed it much.
The conversation ran out before the evening did, and the silence was long.
The candle burned down, but the spark never really took hold.
They parted politely, each privately sure it hadn't been their night.
He checked his pocket watch a few times too many.
Nothing went wrong exactly. Nothing went especially right either.
They both shrugged it off in the hallway and went their separate ways.
She didn't mind saying no.
No hard feelings either way.
She turned him down with a friendly smile and offered him a drink at the bar instead.
She said no politely, and he took it with a gracious nod.
She waved him toward another lady, no offense taken on either side.
She told him honestly it wasn't for her, and he appreciated the honesty.
He asked, she declined, and they went on chatting as if nothing had happened.
She shook her head kindly and the conversation moved on without a hitch.

enc_nomood._note: She turned it down because she wasn't in the mood (low lust).
_default: She just wasn't in the mood.
Not tonight, she said.
She'd had a long day and her heart simply wasn't in it.
She curled up in the corner of the lounge instead, and told him so kindly.
She begged off with a small yawn and a gentler smile.
Maybe another night, she said. Tonight she wanted tea and quiet.
The spark just wasn't there, and she knew better than to fake it.
She wasn't feeling it, so she poured him a drink on the house and let him down easy.

job_bartender._note: Weekly report line for a bartender.
_default: {name} kept the drinks flowing at {house} and settled two arguments with a single raised eyebrow.
{name} invented a new cocktail this week. Half the regulars love it, the other half are scared of it.
{name} worked the bar all week and knows every regular's order by heart now.
{name} polished glasses until they sparkled and served a gruff old sailor who confessed everything. The bar at {house} heard it all.
{name} worked behind the bar of {house} all week, pouring, laughing, and quietly cutting off a very determined merchant.
{name} learned the exact hour that the crowd wants something stronger, and had it ready each time.
A busy week at the bar: {name} juggled three orders at once and still remembered to ask after a regular's cough.
{name} added a pinch of cinnamon to the house wine and had {house} talking about it for days.
{name} turned a dull Tuesday around by sliding free peanuts across the bar and telling a truly terrible joke.

job_dancer._note: Weekly report line for a dancer.
_default: {name}'s new routine had the lounge on its feet.
{name} danced every night this week. Someone threw flowers, which she pretended not to love.
A crowd gathered early for {name}'s set. The bar did well out of it.
{name} danced in the lamplight until her bells jingled, and the room kept time with its feet.
The fiddler struggled to keep up with {name} this week. Nobody minded.
{name} spun through the lounge in silk and shadows, and a few clients forgot to drink.
{name} added a slow, swaying number to her set and the whole room went quiet before it erupted in applause.
Her ankles ached by Friday, but {name} gave the crowd a finale that brought the house down.
{name} dragged a shy client onto the floor for one dance. He talked about it for the rest of the evening.

job_bath._note: Weekly report line for a bath attendant.
_default: {name} kept the baths hot and the guests relaxed.
{name} has the guests so relaxed they forget to leave. She considers it a professional achievement.
Steam, scented oil, and {name}'s soft humming. The bathhouse was busy all week.
{name} kept the water hot and the lanterns low, and the guests drifted out pink and sleepy.
{name} swept steam off the tiles all week and learned to tell a tired merchant from a lonely one by the way he sank into the water.
Fresh towels, cedar oil, and {name}'s quiet humming: the bathhouse had a very good week.
{name} tended the baths and hung herbs from the rafters, which made the whole room smell like a mountain meadow.
The soaking tubs were full every night. {name} says it's the best job she's ever had for her hands.
{name} had the pool so cozy that two guests fell asleep in the water and had to be woken gently.

job_bath_joined._note: Bath attendant comfortable enough to join bathers in the water (bath massage).
_default: {name} didn't just tend the baths this week; she got in. Bath massages, in the water, became the most requested thing on the menu.
{name} spent most of the week in the hot water with the guests, working out knots. Nobody wanted to leave the pool.
Steam, scented oil, and {name} slipping into the water to give massages where they soak. Business was very good.
{name} slipped into the warm water with her sleeves rolled and spent the week kneading shoulders. The steam swallowed every sigh.
{name} traded her towels for a seat in the bath, working knots out of tired backs while lanterns swayed above. The queue was long.
{name} spent the evenings waist-deep in the pool, hands busy and the room fragrant with oil. Guests left looking boneless.
Bath massages from {name}, in the water, with cedar smoke and soft chatter. She says her hands are sore and her heart is full.
{name} dunked herself into the baths each night, and the guests have been tipping like it's a festival.
{name} waded in among the soaking guests this week, and the most-requested spot in the whole house became the one next to her.

job_bath_more._note: Bath attendant who joined bathers and, in the mood, offered them more.
_default: {name} joined the bathers in the water, and once or twice the massage turned into something more, at her suggestion.
Bath massages in the water all week, and {name} was in such a mood that a few lucky guests got more than their backs worked on.
The baths were busy and so was {name}. When the mood took her, the massages didn't stay massages.
{name} slid into the water for massages as usual, but a few times her hands wandered where she meant them to.
The steam was thick, the oil was warm, and {name} was feeling bold. Not every massage stayed innocent.
{name} worked out the knots in tired shoulders, and sometimes the kneading turned into something slower and warmer.
Between the lanterns and the humid hush, {name} let a few of her massages drift further than the menu allows.
{name} treated a few of her favorites to a little extra under the water, and no one was in the mood to complain.
The baths were busy, and so was {name}. A few lucky guests got a massage that ended in a quiet, shared smile.

job_teacher._note: Weekly report line for the classroom teacher.
_default: {name} ran the classroom at {house} with a ruler and endless patience. Notes were taken.
{name} drilled the house until the lesson stuck. Somebody asked for homework. {name} was delighted.
{name} wrote on the slate, pointed, and waited. By evening the whole house was practising.
{name} chalked the day's lesson across the slate at {house} and ran the class with a patient, level voice.
{name} gave the ladies of {house} a hard morning of drills and an easy afternoon of practice.
{name} corrected posture, vowels, and bad habits with a gentle tap of her pointer. By Friday the house was gliding.
{name} turned the classroom of {house} into the liveliest room in the building. Somebody asked for extra lessons.
{name} taught a pupil one tiny trick this week and watched it spread through the house like wildfire.

{name} drops onto the bed with a groan, kicks off her shoes, and wiggles her toes pointedly at you. You get the message and roll up your sleeves.

The parlor has been rearranged into a theater of cushions, and {name} stands at the center like she was born there. She gives the audience a slow look, then turns to you. "Ready, teacher?" she asks, and you forget every word you planned to say.

{name} has brought a pointer, which she does not need and uses constantly. She narrates every step in a clear, cheerful voice, pausing only to correct your posture and to tell the back row to stop whispering. They don't.
By the end, the room is very quiet and very warm. Several of the ladies have taken notes. Some of them are fanning themselves with the notes.
Afterward nobody quite meets anybody's eyes, and everyone has questions. A lot of questions.
There's scattered applause. Someone asks if there'll be a follow-up class. Several people ask, actually.

When it's over, a stunned silence hangs in the air, then breaks all at once into a chorus of impressed murmurs. Two of the ladies are writing frantically, and a third is already asking about next month.
Somebody fans herself with a menu. Somebody else says "Well," in a very small voice, and the entire room agrees that this was a most educational evening.
The audience drifts off in twos and threes, flushed, giggling, and making plans. The cushions will need airing, and so will a few of the spectators.

It starts as a quiet drink in {house} after closing. {names} are all there, and somewhere around the second bottle {first} says what everyone has apparently been thinking. You open your mouth to be sensible. Nobody lets you finish.
{first} knocks on your door with a grin you've learned to be nervous about. Behind her, crowding the hallway: {names}. "We talked it over," she says. "You're outvoted."
Nobody can say afterward whose idea it was. One minute {names} are arguing about who gets your evening, the next someone suggests nobody has to lose, and the argument is over very quickly.

{names} have been whispering in the corner of {house} for an hour, and when {first} finally comes over to your table, the others are right behind her. "We've come to a conclusion," she says. Having learned to dread conclusions, you put your cup down.

It begins with a card game that nobody is playing seriously, and ends with {first} announcing that the stakes have changed. {names} lean in as one. By the time you understand what you've agreed to, the lamps in {house} have been turned down.

The night is warm, the wine is good, and {first} has a gleam in her eye that you recognize from the last three times you lost an argument. "Don't panic," she says, as {names} gather round. "It's a group project."
{a} and {b} end up tangled together more than once and don't seem to mind in the least.
{a} catches {b}'s eye across the bed and they both start laughing, then very much stop laughing.
At one point {a} is coaching {b} with a running commentary. {b} tells her to shut up, then follows every word.
{a} pulls {b} in for a kiss while they wait their turn. It turns out waiting is not the hardship anyone expected.
{a} and {b} have drifted into a corner of their own, trading whispered jokes and soft touches as if they had all night. They do.
Between rounds, {a} straightens {b}'s hair, which immediately ruins it again, and they both grin like thieves.
Much later, the bed is a wreck, the lantern has burned down, and you're pinned under at least three warm, sleeping bodies. You decide this is fine. This is very fine.
By dawn you're all a heap of limbs and sheets. Somebody is snoring. Somebody else is still giggling. You stare at the ceiling, wondering how your life got here, and find you have no complaints.
They drift off one by one. The last one awake is {first}, who props her chin on your chest and says, "Same time next week?" She falls asleep before you can answer.

The candles are stubs, the wine is gone, and the sheets look like they lost a war. You lie in the middle of it, grinning at nothing, as {first} pulls the blanket over all of you. "Goodnight," she says, sleepy and satisfied.

Dawn finds you all tangled, warm, and wholly unrepentant. Birdsong drifts in through the shutters, and {first} is the first to stir, cracking an eye to survey the damage. "Worth it," she mumbles, and goes back to sleep.

The house is silent at last. You take one long look around the room, at the sleeping faces, the scattered cushions, the smile {first} wears even in her sleep, and think that, notes or no notes, you will remember this one.
{name} keeps a hand on you the whole night, sharing you and making very sure everyone knows who you go home with.
{name} stays within arm's reach of you all night, a hand on your shoulder, a foot against your ankle. She shares, but she makes sure everybody knows whose you are when the lamps go out.
Whatever else happens, {name} always ends up back at your side, tucked into the crook of your arm like she belongs there. She does, and she lets the room know it with one sidelong glance.
{name} is generous, laughing, and wonderfully relaxed about the whole affair, but every few minutes her fingers find yours and squeeze. It's a quiet, private message in a very public night.
At some point {name} whispers "mine" in your ear, so softly that only you can hear. Then she turns back to the others with a bright smile and carries on as though nothing at all had been said.
{name} insists on tucking the blanket around you when the night is over, a small, possessive kindness. "You're coming with me," she says, and nobody argues.

private_open._note: Opening of plain private time with you (before the turn and the service line). {name} = her name. Act-neutral.
_default: {name} drags you off for a "lesson." You take notes afterward. She finds this hilarious.
A quiet evening, a locked door, and a "do not disturb" sign that the neighbors would later call unnecessary given the noise.
{name} insists you need more practice. Like a diligent student, you do not argue.
By the time you come downstairs together, everyone has very carefully decided not to look at either of you.

The house has settled into its after-hours hush by the time {name} finds you in the lounge. Rain ticks against the shutters, one lantern is still burning, and she takes the cushion right beside yours instead of across from you. "Walk me upstairs?" she says, as if it were a question.

{name}'s room smells of warm tea and the cedar oil she rubs into the bed frame. She lights a single candle, pulls the curtain against the rain, and pats the quilt beside her. You sit with the care of a man entering a temple.

You start with the leftover plum cakes from the kitchen and a game of cards neither of you is paying attention to. Somewhere around the third hand, {name} puts her cards face down and just looks at you. The candle gutters, and nobody remembers who was winning.

The evening wind pushes the shutters open a hand's width, bringing in night-jasmine and the faraway music of the Silver Fiddle. {name} gets up to close them, changes her mind, and leaves them open. "Better," she says, turning back with a small, private smile.

You knock, which is silly, because {name} invited you and is sitting right there. She raises an eyebrow at the knock, and you apologize, and she laughs until she has to wipe her eyes. It breaks the nervous part cleanly in half, and you are allowed in.

{name} has put a kettle on the little brazier and arranged every cushion in the room into one large, suspicious nest. "Nothing is happening yet," she says, pouring. "This is just the part where we get comfortable." Her foot finds yours under the blanket anyway.

The corridors are quiet, the stairs creak in their usual places, and {name} holds your sleeve all the way up so you don't trip over the loose board. At her door she stops, turns, and straightens your collar for no reason at all. "There," she says. "Now you're presentable. Briefly."

A thunderstorm rolls over Hollowmere just as the last guest leaves, and the whole house goes dim and golden. {name} finds you at your desk, takes the quill out of your hand, and sets it carefully out of reach. "The ledger will survive one night," she says.

You've brought a lantern, a bottle of plum wine, and a plan. The plan dissolves the instant {name} opens the door in her loose robe, her hair half down. She takes the bottle, ignores the plan, and tugs you inside.

The bathhouse steam has drifted all the way up the stairs, and {name}'s skin is still faintly warm and smelling of orange peel when she greets you. She leans in the doorway, in no hurry at all. "I thought you might want some company," she says, "since you've been staring at that door for an hour."

private_first._note: Her first private time with you (replaces private_open once). {name}.
_default:
{name} has clearly been thinking about this. She pulls you into her room before you can finish saying hello.

The door closes.

{name} has clearly been thinking about this. She's tidied her room twice, changed her mind about the lamp three times, and when you arrive she says "Hello" in a very careful voice. Then she laughs at herself and lets you in.

There's a ribbon in {name}'s hair that wasn't there at supper. She doesn't mention it, and having learned some things, you don't either. The room is warm, the lamp is low, and she shuts the door behind you with a soft click and her back flat against it.

"I rehearsed what to say," {name} admits, standing in her doorway with the night breeze in her sleeves. "It was very good. I've forgotten all of it." She takes your hand instead, and her fingers are a little cold and entirely steady.

Rain is drumming on the roof tiles when {name} opens her door, and she's wearing the expression of a woman who has argued with herself for a week and won. She lets you come in, then stands very close, listening to the rain, saying nothing.

{name} has laid out two cups, one candle, and no excuses. She sits on the edge of her bed, folds her hands, then unfolds them. "You're the first person I've actually wanted to ask," she says quietly. "So I'm asking."

private_first_sam._note: Your very first time (replaces private_open once). {name}.
_default:
{name} takes your hand and leads you upstairs. It becomes clear about four seconds in that your previous-life experience in this department is exactly zero.

{name} looks absolutely delighted about this.

The door closes.

You've read about this in two lives and practiced it in neither. You arrive at {name}'s door with your hands clasped like a schoolboy at a recital, and she takes one look at you and smiles so warmly that the nerves lose half their grip. "Come in," she says. "I'll go slowly. I'm very good at slowly."

"I should mention," you begin, in the lamplit hush of {name}'s room, "that I have no idea what I'm doing." {name} puts a finger to your lips, delighted beyond words. "Good," she whispers. "Then nothing gets in the way of me showing you."

{name} takes charge the way she might take a shy guest's coat, gently and without making a fuss of it. She guides your hands, tells you to breathe, and tells you that you don't have to be graceful. The moons are bright in the window, and your ears are the color of boiled shrimp.

You stand at the threshold with the posture of a man about to take an exam. {name} laughs, soft and kind, takes your notebook out of your coat pocket, and sets it on the shelf. "No notes this time," she says, drawing you inside. "Tonight, you just learn it by heart." The door closes behind you.

train_service._note: Hands-on service practice with you (followed by her shown service's private_act line). {name}.
_default: {name} decides your education is a shared project. You work through everything you're both comfortable with, one thing at a time, until both of you are confident in the technique. You take notes afterward. She finds this hilarious.

You bring a candle, a notebook, and the serious face you wear for exams. {name} brings a smirk and a very good memory of what she's comfortable with. You run through her repertoire one item at a time, stopping whenever she says "wait, try it like this," and you write it all down.

It's supposed to be a practice session, and for the first ten minutes it very nearly is. {name} corrects your hand placement, you ask a polite follow-up question, and she tells you that politeness is lovely but you can stop checking in every four seconds. The notes are getting messier.

The practice room smells of lamp oil and warm cedar, and {name} has put cushions everywhere. "Think of it as a rehearsal," she says. You think of it as an exam you're thrilled to be taking. You work through each service she's sure of, polishing and adjusting.

You've drawn a small diagram. {name} looks at it for a long, silent moment, then tells you it's anatomically ambitious and takes the pencil to correct it. After that you do things the hands-on way, and the diagram gets very smudged.

"Rule one," {name} announces, "no giggling at the technique." You break that rule within a minute. Between laughs, you go through each service she's confident in, trading adjustments, and the lamp burns down while you wrestle with the finer points.

The rain beats a steady rhythm on the shutters while {name} walks you through her own repertoire like a guide leading a tour. She stops at each service, shows you what works and what doesn't, and gives you her expert verdict on your form. You scribble frantically, glowing with pride.

train_skill._note: One-on-one trade-skill training, keyed by skill (service, dance, bar, combat, manage; _default fallback). {name}, {skill}. Followed by "Sam takes detailed notes, as is tradition."
_default: You walk {name} through the trade the hands-on way, {skill} first: posture, pacing, the little things regulars notice.

You pull up a stool, and {name} sits across from you with the focused expression she saves for things she wants to be good at. You work through {skill} slowly, one piece at a time, and you're careful to praise what she does well before you mention anything else.

The afternoon light slants across the floor while you and {name} drill {skill} together. She tries it, misses, tries again; you offer a small suggestion; and she gets it on the next go with a bright, startled laugh.

"Show me," you say, and {name} does, and then you show her your own clumsy version for contrast. She's helpless with laughter, which is the best thing that could have happened. After that, {skill} goes much more smoothly.

You keep at {skill} until the lamps need trimming. {name} is stubborn and quick, and you're patient, and somewhere in the middle of it she stops looking at you as the boss and starts looking at you as a very good teacher.
service: You and {name} sit across from each other with a pot of tea and a plan: how to greet a guest, how to read a mood, how to make a tired stranger feel like the only person in the room. She practices her welcome on you four different ways. By the fourth, you're genuinely flustered.

"Eye contact first," you say, "then the smile, then the offer of a drink." {name} nods, tries it, and gets it right on the third go. The lounge is empty and quiet, the afternoon light coming slantwise through the shutters, and she sits a little taller each time you nod.

You spend the afternoon on small things, which turn out to be the big things: how to pour wine without a drip, when to stay silent, when to ask a question. {name} is quick, and the quiet pride on her face grows every time you say "yes, exactly that."

You play the nervous first-time guest. You are, unfortunately, very convincing. {name} manages to settle you with a few well-chosen words and a warm hand on your sleeve, and then you both realize you've forgotten to keep the act up.
dance: The parlor rug is rolled aside and {name} stands barefoot on the boards while you count the beat aloud. You can't dance, but you can spot where her weight drifts, and you've learned to say so gently. She keeps rolling her eyes and correcting herself anyway.

A phonograph does not exist in this world, so you hum and tap the rhythm on a table, badly. {name} laughs, then takes the beat from you and makes it hers, turning slowly across the floor. By the end of the hour, your humming is the only thing out of tune.

"Again from the top," you say, and {name} salutes with a flourish and starts the routine over. Her shadow sweeps long across the wall in the lantern light, and her footwork sharpens every time. She stops at the end, breathing hard, flushed and pleased.

You watch from a stool at the edge of the floor, chin in your hand, offering notes like a very polite critic. {name} adjusts a spin, lifts her arms a touch higher, and the whole thing suddenly flows. You clap once, startled into it, and she bows with a grin.
bar: Behind the empty bar, the shelves of bottles glint in the lamplight. You set out three glasses and a jigger, and {name} learns to measure by eye while you time her pours with a sand-glass. She spills the first one, grins, and wipes the bar with a flourish.

"A good bartender remembers faces," you say, holding up a deck of sketched regulars. {name} studies them, names each one correctly, and adds what each of them drinks. You are unreasonably impressed. She is unreasonably smug.

You go through the shaker, the strainer, and the long spoon, one tool at a time. {name} gets the ice rattle just right on her fifth try, and the sound rings through the quiet room like a small bell. You make her do it six more times, to be sure.

You mix a drink badly on purpose so {name} can fix it. She tastes it, winces, and rebuilds it from the base up, adding a twist of citrus and a pinch of something you don't recognize. It tastes wonderful, and you ask her to show you again.
combat: The yard behind the house is damp from morning rain, and {name} stands in the middle of it with a wooden practice blade in her hand. Thin and nerdy and very serious about this, you demonstrate a stance. She straightens yours, kindly, and then shows you how it's done.

You spar slowly, the wooden blades clacking in the morning stillness. You call out corrections you read once in a book, and {name} humors you for exactly as long as it takes to disarm you. "Theory is lovely," she says, handing your stick back. "Now try it with feet."

{name} runs the drill again and again, footwork first, then guard, then the long step in. You count for her, and the count keeps time with her breathing. By the end her shirt is damp and her grin is sharp.

You don't know a great deal about fighting, but you know how to pay attention. You watch {name} move, notice where she drops her guard, and say so, apologetically. She tests the notion, finds it true, and gives you a surprised look of real respect.
manage: Ledgers, receipts, and a pot of strong tea cover the office desk. You walk {name} through the weekly accounts one column at a time, and she follows with a finger down the page, frowning, then brightening when the numbers click. "So this is where all the candles go," she says.

"A manager's job," you say, "is to make problems small before they're big." {name} considers this seriously, then asks three sharp questions about the rota that you have to look up. She pretends not to enjoy that.

You role-play a difficult guest. You play the guest, loudly and a bit unfairly, and {name} de-escalates you with a calm voice and a firm smile. You fold in under a minute. She sits back, pleased, and takes the last biscuit.

The window is open to the afternoon, with the noise of the street drifting in, and {name} is working out next week's schedule on a slate. You lean over to point out a clash, and she has already spotted it. "Give me some credit," she says, rubbing it out.

_default: You bring {name} {gift}. She turns it over in her hands and tucks it away somewhere safe.
{name} finds {gift} waiting on her pillow, with a note in your careful handwriting.
You hand {name} {gift} without much ceremony. She smiles anyway.
You give {name} a slim velvet box. Inside is a piece that catches the lamplight. She asks you to fasten it for her.
{name} opens the jeweler's box, closes it, opens it again. "You didn't have to," she says, already wearing it.
A pendant from the good shop on the hill. {name} spends the evening finding reasons to touch it.
You have something extravagant delivered for {name}. Half the house comes to look. She pretends not to be thrilled and fails completely.
{name} stares at what you bought her, then at you. "This is too much." She doesn't give it back.
It costs more than some of the furniture. {name} doesn't say much, but she stays close to you for the rest of the night.
Spent her mornings with the {tutor}.
Her {tutor} left her a stack of exercises. She did most of them.
Lessons with the {tutor} went well this week.
